record.title: Preprint couples structural theory revision with diagnostic experiment selection
record.summary: The Oct. 6 preprint proposes a scientific-discovery policy that can revise the hypothesis class itself while choosing experiments designed to distinguish structural edits. In 400 held-out controlled dynamical environments, the authors report 89.5% exact recovery after 32 real experiments, 10 percentage points above their strongest matched baseline. On 200 mechanisms excluded from the edit grammar, they report detecting library insufficiency in 88% of cases with 5.5% false support, and report additional results on ODEBench, ODEBase and DiscoverPhysics. These are author-reported evaluations; no independent reproduction or real laboratory deployment was established in this review.
organizations: University of Science and Technology of China
University of the Chinese Academy of Sciences

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The preprint proposes experimental model-class revision: a policy jointly selects a typed structural edit and a diagnostic experiment, using class-level distinguishability and anytime-valid sequential evidence to decide whether to revise the current hypothesis class.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On 400 held-out controlled dynamical environments, the authors report 89.5% exact recovery at a budget of 32 real experiments, 10.0 percentage points above the strongest matched baseline; the result uses three training seeds and paired test environments.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On 200 mechanisms outside the edit grammar, the authors report library-insufficiency detection in 88% of cases and a 5.5% false-support rate; the paper also reports transfer to ODEBench, ODEBase and DiscoverPhysics tasks.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_LIMITATION
claims.text: The reported outcomes are paper results and do not demonstrate general experimental-science transfer or independent replication; training and teacher-search compute are separate from the reported test-time discovery budget.

evidence_gaps.description: The controlled recovery, insufficiency-detection, ODEBench/ODEBase and DiscoverPhysics results have not been independently reproduced.
The role of grammar choice, teacher-search and policy-training compute, and transfer to noisy real experimental interfaces remains uncertain.

brief.importance_rationale: If the author-reported gains persist beyond controlled and model-library benchmarks, jointly revising a scientific hypothesis space and selecting diagnostic experiments could materially reduce wasted experimentation and improve automated discovery. The reported evidence is not independent and does not establish transfer to laboratory science.
limitations: All performance values are author-reported and were not independently reproduced in this activation.
The main 400-environment benchmark is controlled and synthetic; transfer to real laboratory experiments is not established.
The results depend on a specified typed edit grammar; unrepresented mechanisms can only be detected as library insufficiency within the tested protocol.
Training, teacher-search, and test-time discovery costs are distinct; the 32-experiment budget is not total system cost.
No implementation link or released task manifest was found on the inspected arXiv record; this bounded search does not show that private or unindexed artifacts do not exist.

brief.summary: The Oct. 6 preprint proposes a scientific-discovery policy that can revise the hypothesis class itself while choosing experiments designed to distinguish structural edits. In 400 held-out controlled dynamical environments, the authors report 89.5% exact recovery after 32 real experiments, 10 percentage points above their strongest matched baseline. On 200 mechanisms excluded from the edit grammar, they report detecting library insufficiency in 88% of cases with 5.5% false support, and report additional results on ODEBench, ODEBase and DiscoverPhysics. These are author-reported evaluations; no independent reproduction or real laboratory deployment was established in this review.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report 89.5% exact recovery on 400 held-out controlled dynamical environments with a 32-real-experiment budget, versus 79.5% for the strongest matched baseline. On 200 out-of-grammar mechanisms, they report 88% library-insufficiency detection and 5.5% false support. Additional author-reported evaluation covers ODEBench, ODEBase and DiscoverPhysics.
technical.compute_or_cost: The test-time discovery budget counts real experiments. Appendix E separately accounts for candidate fits and fitting GPU time, and the paper says teacher-search and policy-training compute are additional; the 32-experiment result is not an all-in training-plus-inference cost.
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected arXiv v1 paper documents the proposed method, experimental protocol and reported metrics. the research desk did not run the code or reproduce the evaluations; empirical outcomes remain author-reported.
technical.mechanism: The policy proposes typed edits to the model class together with experiments chosen to distinguish those edits. A shared parameterization must explain the selected experiments, while anytime-valid sequential evidence determines when the current class is rejected. If no admissible edit gains support, the policy can report that its edit library is insufficient.
technical.novelty: The work treats experiment selection and expansion of the hypothesis class as a coupled sequential decision problem, including an explicit outcome for detecting insufficiency in the available edit library.
technical.regime: Controlled dynamical-system discovery with 400 held-out generated environments, 200 out-of-grammar mechanisms, a fixed typed edit grammar and a canonical budget of 32 real experiments; additional model-library and interactive-world benchmarks. The paper reports three training seeds for stochastic methods and paired test environments.
technical.reproducibility: The arXiv HTML paper and protocol appendices were accessible. No paper-specific implementation or task manifest was linked from the inspected arXiv record; no independent reproduction was performed.
technical.strongest_baseline: Falsification plus independent edit/experiment selection under the matched controlled protocol, reported at 79.5% exact recovery versus 89.5% for the joint policy at budget 32.

brief.title: Preprint couples structural theory revision with diagnostic experiment selection
brief.why_it_matters: Scientific discovery systems can fail when every candidate theory shares the same missing mechanism. The paper directly studies that gap by coupling structural revision to diagnostic experiment choice. If its controlled and benchmark results hold under independent testing and transfer to real experiments, this could change how automated discovery systems allocate experiments; current evidence does not establish laboratory impact.
